verses.1: And the Queen of Sheba heard of Solomon’s fame. She came to visit him in Jerusalem, with a very large army and magnificent garments. They wore robes made of gold and precious stones. She went before Solomon and spoke with him about everything that was on her mind.
verses.2: And Solomon told her all her wishes. Nothing from Solomon’s words was left unspoken.
verses.3: And Queen Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, and also the house he built.
verses.4: And he will eat what we have sent him, and he will serve his servants, and he will stand in his positions as a servant. And he will also drink from the vessels that are used for drinking. And on his head there will be a crown that will be placed upon the house of Jehovah. And no evil spirit will ever be able to enter there.
verses.5: And he said to the king, “The truth is what I have heard in my land about your words and your wisdom.”
verses.6: And I did not believe their words until I came and saw with my own eyes. And behold, it seemed to me that half of your wisdom was not enough to explain what I had heard.
verses.7: These are your people and your servants who stand before you always, and they hear your wisdom.
verses.8: May the LORD your God be blessed, who has desired to give you as king on His throne. May He establish Israel as a kingdom forever through His love for you. And He has given you authority over them to rule with justice and righteousness.
verses.9: And she gave the king one hundred and twenty pieces of gold jewelry, along with many precious stones and expensive wood. These were not as valuable as those that the Queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
verses.10: And also the servants of Huraim and the servants of Shlomo, who brought gold from Ophir. They also brought logs of alguim wood and precious stones.
verses.11: And the king made the branches of the alguim trees into columns for the House of God and for the palace of the king. He also made altars and shrines for the priests. But no such things were seen on the land of Judah before.
verses.12: And King Solomon gave to Queen Sheba all the requests she had asked for, along with everything she brought to the king. Then she went back to her own land.
verses.13: And the amount of gold that came to Shlomo in one year was sixty and sixty-six pieces of gold.
verses.14: Besides the people of Tyre and Sidon, all the kings of Arabia and all the people of the land bring gold and silver to Solomon.
verses.15: And King Solomon made a crown of gold. Six ounces of pure gold were used to make this crown. This crown was then placed on the head of one of the kings.
verses.16: And three ounces of blackened gold were used to cover that shield. Three ounces of gold were used to cover one of those shields. The king gave them to him in the house of Lebanon.
verses.17: And the king made a large throne, and it was covered with pure gold.
verses.18: And six poles were set up for the altar, and gold was used to make those poles. They were held in place by hands, one hand on each pole, right next to the altar.
verses.19: And twenty-two years passed there, on those six hills. But this did not happen to any other kingdom.
verses.20: And all the utensils of King Solomon were made of gold. All the objects in the Temple of the Lord were also made of gold. In the time of Solomon, no silver was considered valuable at all.
verses.21: For the daughters of the king went away with the servants of Huraam for three years. They brought back gold and silver, as well as other precious items.
verses.22: King Solomon was the most powerful and wise king of all the kings of the earth.
verses.23: And all the kings of the earth seek to hear the wisdom of Solomon, for God has given him that wisdom.
verses.24: And they bring with them from their offerings all kinds of gold and silver, as well as various kinds of gifts. They also bring horses and other valuable items during each new year.
verses.25: And Solomon had four thousand chariots and horses, along with twenty thousand foot soldiers. He placed them in the cities of the kingdom, along with the king himself in Jerusalem.
verses.26: And he became the ruler over all the kings, from the river down to the land of Philistia, and even as far as the borders of Egypt.
verses.27: And the king gave the money in Jerusalem, as stones. And the acorns were given in their natural state, as they were lying on the ground.
verses.28: And they brought horses from Egypt to Solomon, and from all the lands.
verses.29: And the rest of Solomon’s words, both those earlier and later ones, are not written about the words of the prophet Nathan, nor about the coming of Ahijah the Shilohite. Nor are they related to the prophecy that was made regarding Rehoboam, son of Nabat.
verses.30: And Solomon ruled over all Israel in Jerusalem for forty years.
verses.31: And Solomon lay down with his fathers. He was buried in the city of David, his father’s city. Rehoboam, his son, became king after him.
